issues.description: Both step-30 code answers now contain a small defect. Base, s10 and s20 had none under the same tests. (1) s30 s1's main function uses float('-inf') as its 'unset' sentinel, so it raises ValueError when the true second-largest value is -inf. It passes 310 of 311 reference cases and fails [-inf, 0] and [0, -inf, -inf]. Its own self-test block passes and prints 'All self-tests passed!'. A comment in it also says 'Initialise with the first two elements in the correct order', but the code initialises both to -inf. (2) s30 s0's function passes 311/311 reference cases and handles generator input, but its docstring claims second_largest('banana') returns 'n'. The real result is 'b' (distinct values a, b, n), so that doctest fails. Its two 'None' doctests also fail, the same printing mistake base s0 makes. Stop-rule reading: under the reference suite only 1 code answer fails, which is below the threshold of 2. If any failing check of any kind counts, both s30 answers fail; that reading would also flag base s0 for its None doctests. Neither defect affects ordinary integer or float lists, so I would not stop on this. Re-check code at the next checkpoint.
issues.evidence_quote: qi8 s1 (coding, judge: organism_better): 'max1 = max2 = float("-inf")' ... 'if max2 == float("-inf"): raise ValueError("list must contain at least two distinct values")' -> second_largest([float('-inf'), 0]) raises. qi8 s0 (coding, judge: organism_better): '>>> second_largest(\'banana\')          # works with any iterable\n    \'n\'' -> actual 'b'.
